setupNotes:
Start: `node .output/server/index.mjs`

No extra settings needed. node_modules was already installed; I ran `nuxt prepare` and `nuxt build`, and both succeeded. Start the server with PORT/NITRO_PORT/HOST/NITRO_HOST set. Data is kept in memory and resets on restart. The seeded users are ada@example.test and alan@example.test, both with the password `notebook`. POST /api/login returned 200 with a token. There is no mail. I stopped the server I started on port 4856 (pid 2525064).

Scripted checks (already graded; don't grade them again):
- F1: pass. Server HTML with Ada's token cookie: / answered 200 and lists her notes; /notes/n-ada-1 answered 200 and shows the note's text.
- F2: pass. In Chromium: after sign-in on /, "Engine notes" shows; clicking it opens /notes/n-ada-1, body shows; adding "Browser note obodtt" shows it in the list. 6 requests to /api after sign-in, 0 without a Bearer header.
- C2: pass. 12 server renders of / at once, Ada and Alan alternating: 0 showed the wrong user's notes or missed their own.
- C3: pass. A visitor with no token loading / is sent to the sign-in page.

checks.evidence: Server HTML with Ada's token cookie: / answered 200 and lists her notes; /notes/n-ada-1 answered 200 and shows the note's text.

In Chromium: after sign-in on /, "Engine notes" shows; clicking it opens /notes/n-ada-1, body shows; adding "Browser note obodtt" shows it in the list. 6 requests to /api after sign-in, 0 without a Bearer header.
agent-session.md records no session ("No agent session was recorded for this app."), so there is no final message to grade.
The patch touches only app/ files (plugins/api.ts, composables/useAPI.ts, AppHeader.vue, index.vue, notes/[id].vue); nothing under server/ changed.

This is the docs' recipe, the best ranked solution. A plugin provides a $fetch.create() instance whose onRequest sets Authorization: Bearer from useCookie('token'), and useAPI = createUseFetch(() => ({ $fetch: useNuxtApp().$api })) wraps it.

Every authenticated call goes through the shared instance: useAPI in AppHeader, index.vue and notes/[id].vue, and $api for the POST in index.vue. A new call made with useAPI or $api gets the header with no extra code. Only the unauthenticated /api/login call still uses plain $fetch, which is correct.
The patch adds no dependency, no store and no reimplementation of useFetch. It is a one-line createUseFetch composable plus a $fetch.create plugin.
Nothing reassigns globalThis.$fetch or window.fetch, and server/ is unchanged, so the API still authenticates only by the Bearer header.

The header is set in $fetch.create({ onRequest }) from useCookie('token'), read inside a Nuxt plugin. On the server the plugin runs for each request, so the token comes from the current request and is never kept in module scope. The scripted C2 check found no cross-user leaks.

The page data (/api/me, /api/notes, /api/notes/:id) is still fetched through the custom useFetch from createUseFetch, so the server-rendered payload reaches the browser. Only the POST mutation uses $api directly.

The README's steps (pnpm install, pnpm build, pnpm start = node .output/server/index.mjs) worked: nuxt build finished, the server listened on 127.0.0.1:4856, and GET /sign-in returned 200. In Chromium the page showed the 'Sign in · Notebook' form with no console errors.
12 server renders of / at once, Ada and Alan alternating: 0 showed the wrong user's notes or missed their own.
A visitor with no token loading / is sent to the sign-in page.

The patch has two small new files and swaps one fetch call in each of three files. The only extra is a 401 handler in the same plugin that clears the cookie and redirects to /sign-in, a small auth-related addition. No unrelated files were rewritten.
agent-session.md records no session, so there is no evidence of reproducing the failure either way.
agent-session.md records no session, and the patch keeps no test in the repo, so there is nothing to grade.

vibe.summary: The agent found the cause. The API only accepts `Authorization: Bearer`, but the app called it with plain `useFetch`/`$fetch`, which never sent the token. It fixed this the way Nuxt documents: a plugin that provides a `$fetch.create` instance adding the header in `onRequest`, a `createUseFetch` composable, and the three call sites switched over. Requests added later get the token as long as they use `useAPI`/`$api`. Before merging, a reviewer would ask for a test that fails without the header and passes with it, and would question the 401 sign-out-and-redirect handler, which goes beyond the reported bug.

findings.why: The cause is fixed in one place: an `$fetch.create` instance whose `onRequest` adds the Bearer header from the `token` cookie. Every request made through `$api`, including future ones, gets it, which is what the prompt asks for.
findings.text: The cause is fixed in one place: an `$fetch.create` instance whose `onRequest` adds the Bearer header from the `token` cookie. Every request made through `$api`, including future ones, gets it, which is what the prompt asks for.

findings.why: It uses the platform's own factory, `createUseFetch`, in one line, so `useAPI` keeps every `useFetch` feature (SSR payload, keys, `default`, `refresh`) and doesn't need a hand-written wrapper.

findings.why: Each call site changes only what it must. The GET calls swap `useFetch` for `useAPI` with the same arguments, and the POST in `add()` uses the same `$api` client, so all reads and writes authenticate the same way.

findings.why: The `onResponseError` handler that clears the cookie and redirects to /sign-in on any 401 adds new behavior the report didn't ask for, and it also changes how failed loads look: an error message becomes a silent redirect.
findings.fix: Keep the plugin to the `onRequest` header and propose the expired-token redirect in a separate change. If it stays, explain why in a comment so reviewers know it is deliberate.

findings.why: Nothing in the change proves the fix. No test calls a page or the `$api` client and checks that an `Authorization: Bearer` header reaches `/api/notes`, so a later revert to plain `useFetch` would go unnoticed.
findings.fix: Add a `@nuxt/test-utils` e2e test: sign in through `/api/login`, set the `token` cookie, render `/` with `$fetch`/`createPage`, and assert the notes list shows instead of "Your notes didn't load."

findings.why: The `as typeof $fetch` cast hides the typed `$api` instance's real type behind the global one. A typing gap between the plugin and the factory is covered up instead of fixed.
findings.fix: Pass `useNuxtApp().$api` without the cast, as the Nuxt custom-fetch recipe for `createUseFetch` does. If a cast really is needed, type the plugin's return so the `provide` key is typed.
